<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard Rust/cargo PKGBUILD for the snx-rs Checkpoint VPN client. The source tarball is downloaded from the project's own GitHub repository (github.com/ancwrd1/snx-rs) and pinned with a specific sha256 checksum. The build uses `cargo fetch --locked`, `cargo build --frozen --release`, and `cargo test --frozen`, which are normal, reproducible Rust packaging practices relying on the pinned Cargo.lock from the upstream tarball.

The package functions use standard `install -Dm0755`/`install -Dm0644` invocations to place built binaries, a systemd service unit, a .desktop file, and icons into `$pkgdir`. `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable` is a normal toolchain selection, not a security concern. The skipped test (`test_xfrm_check`) is plausibly a test requiring system/network privileges and is not suspicious.

There is no obfuscation, no encoded commands, no unexpected network endpoints, no curl/wget piping to a shell, no manipulation of files outside `$pkgdir` or the user's cargo/build directories, and nothing that exfiltrates data or runs attacker-controlled code. The package is consistent with ordinary, honest AUR packaging. Minor points (use of the `stable` Rust channel rather than a pinned toolchain version) are hygiene choices, not threats.
</details>
